question:
A junior risk analyst at an Indian asset management company is preparing a slide for newly hired analysts on why and how the firm estimates expected shortfall (ES) alongside VaR for its INR portfolios. The draft slide contains four statements:

I. VaR gives the loss level that will not be exceeded at the chosen confidence level but says nothing about the size of losses beyond it; ES addresses this by estimating the average loss in the tail.

II. ES is the probability-weighted average of tail losses, so for standard normal losses the 95% ES of 2.063 exceeds the 95% VaR of 1.645.

III. ES is estimated by dividing the entire loss distribution into equal-probability slices and weighting each slice’s quantile by a user-chosen risk-aversion function.

IV. When the tail is cut into $n$ equal-probability slices, the VaR at the chosen confidence level itself is the first of the $n$ VaRs that are averaged.

Which of the statements should remain on the slide?

**What ES is, why it exists, and what it is not**

Stem in one line: which of four training-slide statements about ES (motivation, definition, estimation) should remain?

**Concept and theory**

VaR is a quantile. At confidence level $\alpha$ it is the loss that separates the worst (1 $- \alpha$) of outcomes from the rest. Schweser states the limitation plainly: VaR “does not tell the investor the amount or magnitude of the actual loss”; it gives only the threshold. Two portfolios can share the same VaR and have very different losses once the threshold is breached.

A risk consultant at a Swiss private bank is showing the risk committee how an exponential spectral risk measure weights the loss quantiles of a CHF bond portfolio. The weighting function is $\phi_{\gamma}$ ($p$) = $e^{-\text{(1}-p\text{)}/\gamma} /[\gamma$ (1 $- e^{-1/\gamma}$ )$]$, and the committee has chosen $\gamma$ = 0.02. solution:
**Computing an exponential weight**

Stem in one line: $\gamma$ = 0.02; find $\phi$(0.96); the 96% quantile value is given but not needed.

**Concept and theory**

The exponential weighting function (Eq. 1.19) is

$\phi_{\gamma}$ ($p$) = $\frac{e^{-\text{(1}-p\text{)}/\gamma}}{\gamma\left(1 - e^{-1/\gamma} \right)}$
